preconditions.description: The number of test cases is between 1 and 100, inclusive.
The number of nesting places and villages is between m and n, inclusive, and m is less than or equal to n.
The number of bees in each nesting place is between 0 and 10^9, inclusive.
The number of wasps in each nesting place is between 0 and 10^9, inclusive.
The nesting places connected by branches are numbered between 1 and n, inclusive.

preconditions.expression: The sum of n across all test cases is at most 10^5
preconditions.description: The total number of nesting places across all test cases is at most 10^5.

postconditions.expression: The output is a single integer representing the maximum number of villages in which Ugly Wasp wins.
postconditions.description: The output must be an integer that represents the maximum number of villages in which Ugly Wasp can win according to the optimal partition.

invariants.expression: The Oak is a tree structure.
invariants.description: The nesting places and branches form a tree, ensuring a unique simple path between any two nesting places.

invariants.expression: Ugly Wasp always wins in the most number of villages.
invariants.description: The goal is to maximize the number of villages where Ugly Wasp wins, with the condition that Pretty Bee wins in the remaining villages.
